RFC 4301 Section 7.4: "All implementations MUST support stateful fragment checking to accommodate BYPASS traffic for which a non-trivial port range is specified." On Ze's kernel under unmatched discard, with IN BYPASS and DISCARD entries Ze installs on one UDP local port each, a whole and a fragmented cleartext datagram to the bypassed port are delivered, while whole and fragmented datagrams to the discarded port (XfrmInPolBlock) or the Child SA's port (template mismatch) are not; its guest record goes red with spdPolicyParams reverted. The test's reason for sending no lone tail holds: local input reassembles before any policy check, so a lone tail is never delivered whatever the SPD holds. Together with the IPv4 and IPv6 forward tests on Ze's kernel (whole and fragmented bypass datagrams cross, a lone tail and an unnamed port do not, red with spdForwardGathers reverted), the projection units on spdEntryHasTransit, the IN and OUT storage unit and the any-port negative, every direction Ze installs a port-scoped bypass on is observed at packet level. Residual, judged not to void the verdict: IPv6 local delivery is not observed and rests on Linux's INET6_PROTO_NOPOLICY Fragment header and the same family-agnostic installer the IPv4 test drives.
